title: Relation of beta-blocker-induced heart rate lowering and cardioprotection in hypertension
authors: Bangalore S, Sawhney S, Messerli FH
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
followUp: trials with at least one year of follow-up
population: 9 of 22 randomised trials of beta-blockers as first-line therapy for hypertension that reported heart rate: 34,096 patients on beta-blockers, 30,139 on other antihypertensive drugs and 3987 on placebo; search 1966 to May 2008
funder: not read: the publisher page refused access and no archived full text was found.
result: In meta-regression across trials, a lower heart rate at study end, as attained with beta-blockers, was associated with greater risk of all-cause mortality (r = -0.51, p < 0.0001), cardiovascular mortality (r = -0.61, p < 0.0001), myocardial infarction (r = -0.85, p < 0.0001), stroke (r = -0.20, p = 0.06) and heart failure (r = -0.64, p < 0.0001); the same held for the heart rate difference between treatments against the relative risk reduction. The authors conclude that, unlike in myocardial infarction and heart failure, beta-blocker-associated heart rate reduction increased the risk of cardiovascular events and death in hypertension.
